transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-02-25
Start: 14:00 UTC
Duration: 45 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Jordan Patel (Redwood AE), Maya Li (Redwood SE), Alex Moreno (BrightRoute Infra Lead), Priya Kaur (BrightRoute Eng Manager), Samir Desai (BrightRoute SRE)

Summary:
Short sync to follow up on the recent timeout/5xx incidents during the pilot burst last week, review adaptive rate-windowing changes, and decide next actions around KV-cache anomaly that surfaced in canary. Team to agree on a bench plan and required artifacts for RCA.

Topics:
- Incident timeline from 02/23 04:12 UTC
- Adaptive throttling / rate-window tuning
- KV-cache corruption hypothesis and mitigation
- Retry/backoff budgets and client behavior
- Observability gaps: traces, sampling, audit logs

Action items (recap at end also present in metadata):
- See action_items field

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: ok everyone thanks for jumping on, I think we have about 45 minutes. Quick round — Alex, do you want to start with a brief on what you saw during the burst on Tuesday?
[00:18] Alex: yeah thanks Jordan. So at 04:12 we started to see a spike in 502/5xx from the pilot cluster, latencies climbing then a hard wall of timeouts around 04:17. The traffic pattern was a short hotkey burst — a few endpoints got hammered — and retries from the app made it worse, obviously. We saw some weird KV hits that didn't line up with the model prefixes, like stale prefixes returning, which is where the kv cache suspicion is coming from.
[00:50] Maya: when you say stale prefixes, you mean the cached past-request keys returning old KV? can you show an example trace?
[00:58] Alex: yeah I'll pull one after, but in the trace the KV lookup returned a key that matched a previous user session, not the current prompt id — sounded like a race when the cache was being refreshed. Could be a locking/tombstone issue when we evict entries under pressure.
[01:20] Priya: and that lines up with the timeline where we saw an increase of retries from clients — the client SDK did exponential backoff but the default window was too narrow, so it retried into the same overloaded pool.
[01:34] Samir: plus our infra had a short GC pause that coincided with the plume, so some requests queued and then timed out, creating that sharp 5xx spike.
[01:44] Jordan: okay, good. So multiple contributing factors: hotkey surge, kv-cache anomaly, retry pile-on, and an infra pause. Maya, any preliminary thoughts from Redwood side on mitigating kv-cache race?
[01:58] Maya: we have a couple of mitigation paths: 1) stronger cache consistency ops — make invalidation synchronous for that key range during rollouts, 2) change eviction policy to prefer LRU with a stronger per-model namespace quota, or 3) bypass cache for critical endpoints during canary. All have tradeoffs — sync invalidation increases latency, bypass increases cost, eviction tuning is low-risk and worth trying first.
[02:27] Priya: eviction tuning — what knobs would you propose? We need something that doesn't regress tail latency under normal traffic.
[02:34] Maya: set per-shard quotas and then a short probation TTL for newly cached items. Also limit concurrent cache refreshes — a single-flight fetch per key to avoid stampede. That helped a different customer with similar pattern.
[02:51] Alex: single-flight would help. Also, is there an option to add a small jitter on client retry so they don't all hammer at the same backoff boundary?
[02:59] Jordan: yeah, we can recommend jitter and a slightly increased initial backoff. But there's also the adaptive rate-windowing change we rolled last week — quick status on that, Maya?
[03:12] Maya: the adaptive windowing was intended to reduce reject rate by widening the token window when throughput drops, but our telemetry shows it kept the window narrow under this burst because it relies on smoothed metrics; the short hotkey spike fooled it. We need faster reaction — shorter smoothing or an emergency widen threshold triggered by queue depth.
[03:34] Samir: shorter smoothing is fine, but we also want predictable ceilings. If the window widens too fast we risk overloading the downstream model instance. Maybe pair it with a graceful shedding policy that routes overflow to a cheaper model variant.
[03:49] Priya: routing to a cheaper variant is acceptable for non-critical endpoints; product will accept lower quality fallback. But for auth flows we need 100% fidelity.
[03:58] Jordan: good note — routing policy needs per-route config. We'll add per-route fallbacks in the config we send you.
[04:06] Alex: what about observability — we didn't have fine-grained sampling for the KV lookups. We saw a few traces but not enough to reproduce. Can Redwood enable higher sampling or a capture mode for a 2h window?
[04:18] Maya: yes we can enable trace capture on the pilot cluster and increase KV lookup logging for a limited window; that will add overhead so we'll gate it to a maintenance window. We'll put the capture window into the runbook.
[04:30] Priya: that'll help. Also we need the audit logs for auth tokens and SSO events around the incident — per security team request.
[04:38] Jordan: we have SSO/SAML and audit docs, will include them. anything else on security checklist?
[04:44] Samir: KMS usage — are keys rotated during our pilot? We saw unusual KMS latency around the incident but haven't tied it to anything.
[04:52] Maya: we don't rotate keys in-flight for the pilot, but if your KMS added latency it's possible it affected token validation path; we'll correlate logs.
[05:00] Alex: back to retry budgets — our app currently has a client-side retry policy of 5 attempts with 100ms base; that seemed high in practice. We want a recommended policy from Redwood for high-QPS environments.
[05:12] Jordan: for this workload we typically recommend 2 retries with randomized jitter, initial backoff 200ms, and circuit-breaker on 5xx rate > X over Y seconds. We'll send a sample SDK patch.
[05:23] Priya: can you include guidance for burst smoothing like token bucket limits on the client side? We can throttle front load from the app if needed.
[05:30] Maya: yes, client-side token bucket + server-side adaptive windowing should work together. We'll add a recipe to the runbook.
[05:38] Alex: one more item — during the incident we saw an increase in 429s from the control plane when we hit rate limits, but rate limits are hard to tune because of variable payload sizes. Any suggestions on metering?
[05:50] Jordan: meter on tokens consumed rather than request counts; Redwood supports per-token rate-limiting and per-route quotas. We'll propose an initial quota based on your token-distribution sample.
[06:01] Samir: can we also get alert thresholds that map to user-visible SLAs? Right now our ops are alerted on infra metrics only.
[06:09] Maya: yes, we'll recommend alert rules for P95 latency, queue depth, KV miss rate, and error budget burn rate. We can pre-populate Grafana dashboards for you.
[06:21] Alex: timeline to next steps — what can we expect to get from Redwood by Monday?
[06:26] Jordan: we'll produce: 1) runbook with retry and client guidance, 2) KV-cache mitigation proposal (eviction configs, single-flight), 3) suggested token quotas and fallback routing plan, and 4) trace capture schedule.
[06:40] Priya: BrightRoute will: provide sample traces and token distribution, and carve out a 2h maintenance window for trace capture. We'll also push a small client SDK tweak to reduce retries.
[06:51] Jordan: great. any blockers on delivering the runbook quickly?
[06:55] Maya: none, but we need the sample traces to tune quotas. If you can't share them, we'll run synthetic hotkey tests against a mirror.
[07:05] Alex: we can share sanitized traces and a simple traffic dump.
[07:10] Priya: ok, for scheduling the KV deep-dive, week of March 8 works for the team.
[07:16] Jordan: perfect. last bit — do we want to enable a temporary bypass so critical auth endpoints skip cache for the next 48h while we stabilize?
[07:26] Samir: yes let's do that for auth only.
[07:29] Jordan: noted.
[07:31] Maya: I'll open a change request and tag you all, set the capture window, and start drafting the runbook. Jordan will send pricing note for the increased capture overhead.
[07:41] Jordan: ok I'll follow up with pricing and the runbook. thanks everyone.
